# Patina

> Patina is a deterministic-simulation runtime for Rust. It runs ordinary `std`
> programs (single Rust sources or whole Cargo packages)
> under a cooperative scheduler, a virtual clock, an in-memory filesystem, and a
> simulated network, so every run is a pure function of a seed. Runs are recorded
> to a trace and replayed byte-for-byte. Seed-driven fault injection (crashes,
> torn writes, network loss/jitter, sleep jitter) and a FoundationDB-style
> cooperative-SUT SDK (`buggify!`) turn a normal test into a deterministic
> distributed-systems fuzzer. Everything below is the `patina` CLI surface
> and is verified against the current build.

Patina has no host fallback: a supported `std` call is deterministic or the run
fails closed (a missed interposer is a refusal, never a silent escape). A trace
carries its seed, fault config, and buggify config, so `replay` is flag-free.

## Install

- Tool: `curl -fsSL https://github.com/JacobHayes/patina/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh`
  installs `~/.local/bin/patina` (append `-s -- --version X.Y.Z` or
  `--prefix DIR`); or `mise use -g github:JacobHayes/patina`. Released for
  Linux x86_64 and arm64 and macOS arm64.
- The machine supplies the guest's toolchain: Rust 1.99+ and `cc` for every
  guest, Go for `--go`, `make`/`curl`/`tar` for `--python`.
- Rust SDK: `patina-dst = { git = "https://github.com/JacobHayes/patina", tag = "vX.Y.Z" }`
  (`features = ["macros"]` for `#[patina_dst::test]`). Go SDK:
  `go get github.com/JacobHayes/patina/go/patina@vX.Y.Z`. Use the tag of the
  installed tool (`patina --version`): a package build refuses an SDK from
  another release line by name.

## Targets

Every run is native and interposed: a Mach-O/ELF binary linked against the shim
runs as is, and a `.rs` file, package directory, or `Cargo.toml` is built
shim-linked on the fly, then run. `test <DIR|Cargo.toml>` rebuilds one libtest
target shim-linked.

A verb's flags are machine-readable: `patina <verb> --help --format json`
lists every flag group (tagged with the forms that accept it where a verb has
several, e.g. the `trace` subcommands), plus `requires` for a flag that is inert
without another. A flag given to the wrong form is refused by name, not as an
unknown option.

Every flag except `--help`/`--version` can be defaulted from `PATINA_<FLAG>`:
`PATINA_` plus the long name in upper snake case (`--seed-start` ->
`PATINA_SEED_START`), shown as `[env: ...]` in help and as `env` in the JSON
registry. A typed flag wins, then a non-empty variable, then the built-in default
(a typed flag also beats a variable for a flag it is mutually exclusive with). A
switch reads `0/false/no/off/n/f` as off and anything else as on. A variable
defaults its flag only where that flag is accepted, and the children a campaign
or minimize spawns never inherit one. `PATINA_RT_*` is the runtime's internal
control plane: only the supervisor sets it, and an inherited one is stripped.

## CLI verbs

- `patina build <SOURCE.rs|DIR|Cargo.toml> [--output PATH] [--release] [--instrument]`
  Build a deterministic shim-linked artifact. `--instrument` adds an LLVM
  SanitizerCoverage hook at every edge: it keeps edge counters (`--coverage-out`,
  `coverage`, `campaign --guided`) and takes the scheduling points a run's
  `--yield-stride N` asks for, one every N edges a thread executes, so
  atomics-only race windows become schedulable (1 = every edge, the densest and
  most expensive; the default 0 adds none). The stride is recorded in the trace
  and a replay takes it from there; an instrumented binary folds `+instrumented`
  into the compatibility fingerprint and a non-zero stride `+yieldstride`.
  Prints `PATINA_BUILD output=...`.
- `patina build <GO PACKAGE DIR> --go [--go-test] --output PATH [--release] [-- GO BUILD OPTIONS]` (`--go-test`: the package's test binary, `go test -c`)
  Build a Go main package as a native guest (Linux): `go build` in cgo mode
  (`CGO_ENABLED=1`), linked externally with the shim, so goroutine threads
  start through the shim's `pthread_create`. Patina sets `-ldflags` and `-o`
  and refuses them in the pass-through options; other `go build` options pass
  through. The `go` on PATH builds it (pin it with `GOTOOLCHAIN` or mise).
- `patina build <SCRIPT.py|DIR> --python --output PATH [--python-path DIR]... [--python-source TARBALL|DIR] [--release]`
  Build a Python application (a script, or a directory with `__main__.py`)
  as a native guest: CPython built statically by Patina's recipe (the pinned
  release fetched once and digest-checked, or `--python-source`) and cached,
  with the standard library, the application and each `--python-path` root (a
  virtualenv's site-packages; earlier roots shadow later ones) frozen into the
  executable. The interpreter is isolated and imports nothing from a
  filesystem. Pure-Python only: an extension module refuses the build; package
  data is not carried; `zlib` is built in, `ssl` is not. Linux only. Every
  guest has the Python SDK, `import patina` (inert under plain Python with
  `crates/cargo-patina/python/sdk` on the path).
- `patina run <ARTIFACT|SOURCE> [--seed N | --record PATH] [--coverage-out PATH] [FAULT OPTIONS] [--buggify] [-- ARGS]`
  Run under the deterministic runtime. `--seed` (default 0) drives everything.
  `--record PATH` writes a trace. `--env K=V` sets the guest's starting
  environment, `--cwd PATH` its starting working directory (an absolute path
  that must exist in the deterministic image; default `/`), and `--param K=V` a
  run parameter it reads through `patina_dst::param`; all are recorded into the trace and restored flag-free
  on replay.
  `--realtime-epoch 2001-09-09T01:46:40Z` sets realtime at
  monotonic zero (default 2026-07-22T23:00:09Z, Patina's first commit), not
  guest-start wall time. The default boot origin is 12345.678901234s of uptime;
  realtime = epoch + uptime, so default guest start is 2026-07-23T02:25:54.678901234Z.
  RuntimeConfig can override the nonzero origin; traces record and restore it.
  `--hostname NAME` sets the node name `uname`/`gethostname` report (default
  `patina`, at most 64 bytes); both are recorded and restored flag-free on
  replay.
  Native `--instrument` binaries emit
  `PATINA_COVERAGE_REPORT`; `--coverage-out PATH` writes a `patina.covmap/v1`
  edge-counter map and refuses plain native binaries with a
  `build --instrument` hint; `--yield-stride N` on a plain binary is refused
  the same way.
  Native runs execute with address-space randomization off; a host that
  forbids it (Docker's default seccomp profile) refuses the run unless
  `--allow-randomized-address-layout` is passed (also on `test` and
  `campaign`, which forwards it to every generation and
  reproduce command). It keeps the host's layout, pads nothing, qualifies the
  run (stderr warning, envelope `qualifications[]`) and records
  `address_layout: "randomized"` in the trace, where a fixed run records
  `"fixed"`. Its replay needs the flag too, as does a trace with no
  `address_layout` (recorded before layout control, so randomized); a
  fixed-layout trace's replay must not pass it, and a standalone (unsupervised)
  replay of a fixed trace is refused. A native campaign's state records its
  layout policy; one without it predates layout control and is not continued.
  A guest stack limit the host
  cannot apply stops the run as `internal`, `stop.reason` `host_limit`.
- `patina test [DIR|Cargo.toml] [TESTNAME] [--exact] [-p NAME]... [--workspace] [--lib] [--bin NAME]... [--bins] [--test NAME]... [--tests] [--skip-target NAME]... [--skip PATTERN]... [--include-ignored] [--seed N | --seeds N] [--jobs N] [--timeout-secs S] [--accept-unsupported TEXT]... [--no-run] [--release] [--instrument] [RUN/FAULT/BUGGIFY/SCHEDULE/LIVENESS OPTIONS]`
  A package's own libtest suite, unmodified: selection is `cargo test`'s
  (default: the package in DIR, else the workspace's default members; lib,
  bins and integration tests). Each selected target is built shim-linked once
  and staged at `target/patina/dst/PACKAGE/KIND/TARGET/guest` (`--no-run`
  builds and prints the staged paths); its tests are listed under the
  runtime, and each test runs on each seed as its own `patina run` child in a
  world of its own, `--jobs` at a time (default: half the usable CPUs), the
  trailing filter and each `--skip` a substring or with `--exact` the whole
  name (libtest's rules); `--skip-target NAME` leaves out a whole target. `#[ignore]` tests are skipped
  unless `--include-ignored`; `#[should_panic]` is libtest's. One verdict per
  test: the class of its lowest failing seed (seeds above it are not run), or
  `ok`. A finding is rerun recorded to `<stage>/traces/NAME.seed-N.patina`; a
  rerun that ends otherwise makes the test `nondeterministic`. A test still
  running after `--timeout-secs` (default 300) is `timeout`. Exit: 0 when all
  pass or are skipped, 1 on any finding, 2 when a test or target could not run
  (`unsupported`, `timeout`, a build failure) or the filter matched nothing.
  `--accept-unsupported TEXT` keeps an `unsupported` test whose stop names TEXT
  from raising the exit status; it still reports as `unsupported`, never `ok`.
  Human output: progress per test on stderr, then counts per class and, per
  non-ok test, its class, one line of why, `rerun:` and `replay:` commands.
  `--format json` prints `schema: "patina.test/v1"` with `counts`, `targets`
  and per-test `result`, `attribution`, `seed`, `seeds_passed`, `duration_ms`,
  `why`, `stop`, `guest_exit`, `likely_artifacts`, `rerun`, `replay`, `trace`,
  plus `build_seconds` and `run_seconds`. A test's `likely_artifacts` (the run
  envelope's, below; a `--timeout-secs` backstop adds a `patina_limit`) also
  print under it in the human summary and mark its progress line. A test that
  reads a fixture by absolute path (`env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")`) needs it
  mounted at its own path: `--mount $PWD:$PWD`.
- `patina replay <ARTIFACT|SOURCE> <TRACE> [--coverage-out PATH] [host inputs]`
  Reproduce a recording. Flag-free: seed, fault knobs, buggify, and guest argv
  are restored from the trace (the trace is authoritative; a re-supplied semantic
  flag that conflicts is refused). A fingerprint or operation mismatch fails
  closed with a nonzero exit. A native trace also carries its build identity
  (`metadata.native`: the executable's and the `patina` executable's
  digests, plus the patina version, shim bundle and target as context, stamped
  by the supervisor when it commits the recording); replay against a different build, or of a
  trace with no identity, is refused before the guest starts, naming each
  differing component (`error`, `stop.reason` `trace_mismatch`).
- `patina trace info <TRACE>` / `trace events <TRACE> [--kind LIST] [--task SEL]... [--seq A..B] [--first N|--last N] [--notable]` / `trace stats <TRACE>` / `trace diff <A> <B> [--context N]`
  Inspect an existing trace without executing a guest. `info` prints metadata,
  resolved event count, and virtual-time span. `events` prints the
  shared decoded event view; `--kind` accepts operation tags or categories
  (`filesystem`, `network`, `scheduling`, `sleep`, `clock`, `entropy`, `crash`,
  `other`), and `--task` accepts a task id or `main`. `stats` aggregates totals,
  per-kind/category/task counts, notable events, and a virtual-time histogram.
  `diff` compares two traces, exits 0 when identical and 1 when metadata/events
  diverge, and reports the first operation/outcome/length divergence. A metadata
  field that is an object on both sides is diffed by member (`native.executable_sha256`).
- `patina audit <ARTIFACT|SOURCE> [--allow SYMBOL]...`
  Strict fail-closed import allowlist. Any un-interposed effect symbol is a
  finding. Audit source-first (or a `patina build` artifact): only a
  shim-linked binary shows the true post-interposition residual, so a stock
  prebuilt binary is refused unless `--raw`.
- `patina campaign <ARTIFACT|SOURCE> [--gens N] [--out-dir DIR] [--spec FILE.json] [--seed-start N] [--plateau-after N] [--guided] [--allow-unmet-sometimes] [--vary DIM,...] [--fault-scale-permille N] [--swarm] [--dns-entry NAME=ADDR]... [--liveness-watchdog NANOS] [--converge-within NANOS] [--no-verify] [--allow SYMBOL] [--allow-unsupported-symbols all|name,...] [--allow-randomized-address-layout] [--cpus N] [--mount HOST_DIR[:GUEST_DIR]]` (`--mount`: the corpus every generation captures, at GUEST_DIR or `/`, forwarded to every reproduce command)
  Config-driven deterministic fault-and-schedule sweep: every generation's seed
  and knobs are a pure function of the generation number. `--vary DIM,...`
  names what each generation draws: `buggify` (fresh fire odds), `sched-pct`
  (a PCT depth), `yield-stride` (a stride from 1 to 1024), and fault planes.
  `faults` bands every
  fault plane's knobs — `fs` (error/short/latency), `crash` (independent
  per-operation machine and process crash rates; native-only),
  `net` (drop/latency/jitter/duplicate/connect-refuse/reset/TCP buffer), `dns`,
  `entropy`, `sleep` (sleep jitter) and `epoch` (realtime-epoch jump) — so
  successive generations explore different fault shapes. `--vary net,sleep`
  (spec key `"vary": ["net", "sleep"]`) draws only the named planes, at the
  values an every-plane campaign draws, for a guest that needs a plane always
  off; an unknown dimension is a usage error. The list is recorded in the out-dir
  spec, so a continuation, the reproduce commands and
  `minimize --generation` keep it, and `--swarm` masks within it. The spec key
  `"exclude_knobs": ["--net-reset-permille", ...]` turns single knobs of a
  selected plane off, for a guest that models only some of its faults; a name
  that is not a drawn fault knob, or whose plane is not selected, is
  refused, and the exclusion is recorded in the out-dir spec. `--dns-entry`
  (repeatable) is campaign SHAPE, not a per-generation draw: it records the host
  table in the out-dir spec, forwards it to every generation, and is what enables
  the DNS band (fail per-mille + resolution latency) — with no defined name every
  lookup is NXDOMAIN by semantics and the knobs could not fire, so the band is not
  emitted at all. `--allow
  SYMBOL` (repeatable), and `--allow-unsupported-symbols` are campaign SHAPE in
  the same sense: the native `run` invocation is forwarded verbatim to every
  generation, so a guest that needs the pre-run gate
  hatch can be swept at all instead of being refused identically in every
  generation. They also ride on the reproduce commands, since a trace cannot
  carry them; a non-native campaign carrying one is refused by name. Each
  generation lands in the class its own `patina.result/v2` envelope reports
  (`result`; the outcome table below), never read from guest output text. The
  campaign overrides it only with what it alone knows: its wall-clock backstop
  is `timeout`, a generation killed from outside or one that reported no run is
  `internal`, and a clean run whose fault plane went inert is `vacuous`. A guest
  that never calls the verdict ABI declares its own rules in the spec
  (`classify.patterns` = class -> output substrings, `classify.exit_codes` =
  class -> guest exit codes); declared rules only ADD a finding where the run
  reached none (`ok`, or a bare `failure`) and can never downgrade one. Before a novel
  finding signature is reported its reproduce command runs once (replay of the
  saved trace, else the seeded re-run), and a seeded one-in-16 sample of clean
  generations runs twice. The comparison is exact, not by signature (which
  collapses numbers): a differing signature, exit status, unnormalized finding
  line (a `PATINA_INFRA native_run` line loses its trace path and scratch-file
  reason), verdict row (detail included) or
  trace digest, or a replay that does not follow its trace (`replay_divergence`
  in the replay's envelope), is `nondeterministic` — the one cross-run class,
  reported with both outcomes
  (`verification` on the signature and notable run, a `verification` summary
  in the envelope). Any other reproduction that ends inconclusive (`timeout`,
  `internal`, `error`) is counted apart and keeps the observed class; `--no-verify` skips the
  extra runs. Novel failure
  signatures are deduped with saved
  traces, SDK site coverage is folded into `<out-dir>/sites.json` (schema
  `patina.campaign.sites/v1`), and native edge coverage (`--instrument`, or a Go guest) is folded
  into `<out-dir>/coverage/` (schema `patina.coverage.campaign/v3`) with a
  plateau report controlled by `--plateau-after`. Unsatisfied `sometimes!`/
  `reachable!` oracle sites, including link-time-declared rows with
  `registered_gens=0`, fail the campaign by default unless explicitly waived.
  `--guided` steers generations instead of deriving them independently: a
  generation may be a local mutation of a corpus entry (an earlier generation
  that first covered an edge), keeping its seed
  and every knob except one to three re-drawn or nudged units (the seed, or a
  knob the spec reads). Entries are picked by energy, which favours rare,
  little-mined finds, and the exploit share follows which arm has recently been
  finding novelty. It stays deterministic (a pure function of seed base,
  generation, and the persisted edge and decision logs; a resumed campaign
  reuses a recorded decision), records the per-generation decision on the
  `PATINA_CAMPAIGN_GEN` line as `guided=exploit:<gen>|explore|none`, and is
  refused when the artifact supplies no novelty signal. `mise run bench:guided`
  compares it with the default sweep, paired, over many seed bases: guidance
  finds a bug behind nested knob thresholds sooner, but not the workq bugs,
  so prefer the default sweep unless the target has that shape.
  The same campaign command given again for its out-dir continues the recorded
  campaign: it finishes an interrupted one, runs the missing generations when
  `--gens` is larger, and otherwise runs nothing and reports the recorded
  result with the same exit status. A command for another artifact or other
  settings is refused, naming what differs. Without the artifact,
  `patina campaign [--out-dir DIR] [--gens N]` continues the recorded campaign
  as it is. Every generation's seed, run flags, class and verdicts are appended
  to `<out-dir>/generations.jsonl`. A spec key is its flag's name in snake
  case (`"gens"`, `"seed_start"`, `"vary"`, `"dns_entry"`, `"allow"`, ...).
- `patina coverage <BINARY> <MAP|CAMPAIGN-OUT-DIR> [--focus CRATE::module] [--top N]`
  Read-only offline symbolization for native edge coverage (`--instrument`, or a
  Go guest). Resolves covmap PCs from the `patina_yield_point` anchor, demangles
  symbols, rolls edges up by crate/module/function (a Go edge, which has no pc,
  by its package only), refuses campaign stores whose recorded artifact
  hash does not match `<BINARY>`, and emits human tables or a
  `patina.coverage/v1` JSON envelope.
- `patina minimize --generation N [--out-dir DIR] [--marker TEXT] [--output PATH] [--jobs N]`
  Reduce one failing campaign generation: delta-debug the fault-knob
  vector that generation drew (each candidate a fresh seeded `run`), print and
  write the standalone reproduction command to `DIR/minimized/generation-N.repro`,
  then record the minimal-knob run as a trace that replays without flags. Patina's own
  oracle needs no hand-written failure text: it targets the `verdicts` the
  campaign recorded for that generation in `campaign-state.json`
  (`patina.campaign.state/v4`), and a candidate still fails only when its replay
  reports every one of those `(kind, label)` pairs. Only
  failure verdicts (`violation`, `abort_intent`) are targeted — a `pass` reports
  that a property held, which is not a failure to preserve — and `detail` is
  never matched. `--marker TEXT` (`A|B` matches either) overrides the target with
  literal output text, for a guest that reports nothing through the verdict ABI;
  a generation with no failure verdict and no `--marker` is refused by name,
  and so is a `nondeterministic` generation, `--marker` or not: its failure is
  that two runs disagree, which no single-run oracle can preserve.
  Because that oracle is hermetic by construction, candidates are evaluated in
  parallel by default (`--jobs`, default half the CPUs).
- `patina minimize --params -- patina run <BINARY> --param K=V... [RUN OPTIONS] [-- ARGS]`
  Shrink the `--param` set of a failing command: each candidate drops or
  shrinks a parameter (numbers toward zero, values toward empty) and re-runs
  the command; it still fails when it exits with the original's non-zero
  status. Prints `PATINA_MINIMIZE_PARAMS_COMPLETE params=[...] oracle_runs=N
  repro: <command>`.
- `patina syscalls`
  Print a target-local kernel-entry inventory and its C symbol layer (default:
  this host). Linux x86_64/aarch64 rows carry runtime dispositions; Darwin
  aarch64 inventories pinned BSD, Mach, ARM-special and platform entries,
  preserving guarded alternatives and invalid slots by name without claiming raw-entry models.
  Darwin x86_64 is not inventoried. Shared JSON schema: `patina.syscalls/v3`.
  Row identity is `(namespace, nr, subcode)`; `variants` name each source alternative.
  Linux runtime fields are under each row's `linux` object (`disposition`,
  `closes_in`, `since`, etc.); ABI is `metadata.linux.virtual_abi`. Darwin has no virtual ABI;
  `darwin.raw_entry` is `not-interposed`, independent of C symbol status.
  MIG messages and commpage APIs are outside the kernel-entry scope.

## Fault + buggify knobs (seed-driven, default off)

- `--machine-crash-permille N`, `--process-crash-permille N`, `--fs-error-permille N`, `--fs-error-at KIND:N[:ERRNO]` (repeatable; the Nth op of a kind fails at any seed), `--fs-short-permille N`, `--fs-latency-nanos MIN..MAX`
- `--sleep-jitter-nanos MIN..MAX`, `--net-jitter-nanos MIN..MAX`, `--net-drop-permille N`, `--net-latency-nanos N`
- `--dns-entry NAME=ADDR` (repeatable), `--dns-fail-permille N`, `--dns-latency-nanos MIN..MAX`
- The knobs above are accepted by `run` and `test` and refused by `replay`,
  which restores them from the trace. Campaigns draw the crash knobs from the
  `crash` plane. A crash restarts the guest once with the same arguments and
  environment and no restart signal: it learns it restarted only from the disk.
- `--buggify`, `--buggify-fire-permille N`, `--buggify-activation-permille N`, `--buggify-cutoff-nanos N`, `--buggify-after-setup` (each detail knob implies `--buggify`)

## Output options (all verbs; stripped before routing, never reach the guest)

- `--format human|json` (default human). `json` usually prints ONE result
  envelope on stdout (schema `patina.result/v2`) and folds captured guest output
  into it; `coverage --format json` emits `patina.coverage/v1`, and `trace
  events --format json` is the streaming exception and emits
  `patina.trace.events/v1` JSON Lines. Human output is unchanged by default.
  NOTE: the selector is `--format`, not
  `--output`, because `--output PATH` is already the build/minimize artifact path.
- `--progress` (opt-in, needs `--format json`; human output always shows its
  own progress): while `run`, `campaign` or `test` works, stream progress on
  stderr as JSON Lines, schema `patina.progress/v1`. Every line is one object
  with `schema`, `verb`, `event` and `elapsed_secs` plus the event's fields:
  `build_started`/`build_finished`, `run_started` (`seed`), `campaign_started`
  (`done`, `target`), `generation` (`done`, `target`, `failures`,
  `novel_signatures`, `classes`; sent for every failing or novel generation,
  every `--progress-every` generations and the last one), and `test_finished`
  (`done`, `total`, `failures`, `class`). stdout still carries the one result.
  Lines without the schema are diagnostics (a cargo warning, say).
- `--verbose` / `-v`: a run's end-of-run reports (`PATINA_*_REPORT`, their
  `PATINA WARNING`s), the pre-run gate's notes and
  cargo's progress. Without it a run prints the guest's output, a one-line
  warning when requested faults never landed, and the result line. Verdicts,
  violation markers and refusals print either way. Under `--format json` the
  reports are the envelope's `reports` field, never part of `stderr`.
- `--render OUT.html` (run or replay; a run without `--record` records to a
  scratch trace for the page): write a self-contained,
  single-file HTML timeline — per-task lanes over trace sequence, colored by
  category (scheduling, sleep, network, filesystem, crash, entropy, clock), a
  metadata panel rendered generically from the trace JSON, per-task rollups, and
  a notable-events list (crashes, boundary errors, dropped datagrams). No
  external assets. Large traces aggregate into density buckets with a visible
  banner. Rendering only reads the trace, so it never changes a replay hash.
- `--report OUT.html`: like `--render` but only on failure; the page leads with a
  failure summary (what fired, exit code, the result/violation lines).

### JSON result envelope (`patina.result/v2`)

One line of JSON on stdout. Always: `schema`, `verb`, `result`, `exit_code`,
and `attribution` unless the result is `ok`. `result` is the one outcome class
`run`, `test`, `replay` and `campaign` share, and `attribution` and `exit_code`
are functions of it:

| `result` | `attribution` | `exit_code` | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ok` | (absent) | 0 | finished, nothing found |
| `violation` | `guest` | 1 | `always!`, a `violation` verdict, a spec-declared class, an SDK contract the guest broke |
| `liveness` | `guest` | 1 | the liveness/convergence watchdog, or a deadlock |
| `failure` | `guest` | 1 | the guest exited nonzero (a panic included) |
| `crash` | `guest` | 1 | the guest died on a signal |
| `unsupported` | `patina_unsupported` | 2 | the guest did something Patina does not model; `stop.detail` names it |
| `timeout` | `patina_unsupported` | 2 | the compute bound, `--budget` or a campaign's backstop ran out |
| `nondeterministic` | `patina_internal` | 2 | a replay left its trace; a campaign reproduction did not reproduce |
| `internal` | `patina_internal` | 2 | Patina failed, or the host took the run away |
| `vacuous` | `request` | 2 | a configured fault plane had nothing to act on (campaign only) |
| `error` | `request` | 2 | usage, build, a missing or mismatched input |

The class is derived from the structured fields below only (the runtime's
facts, the shim's stop record, the guest's wait status); printed failure text
alone is a `failure`. `exit_code` is the tool's own exit status, never the
guest's (`guest_exit`). A campaign's exit status is 1 when any generation is a
finding in the guest or its coverage gate fails, else 2 when any generation is
not clean. When applicable: `artifact`, `fingerprint`, `seed`, `render`,
`reproduce` (the command that repeats a run that did not end clean: the replay
of its recording, else the `run` with its seed spelled out), `findings`
(audit import/finding strings), `finding_details` (structured audit symbol,
category, provenance), `output_path` + `content_hash` (build), `verdicts` (every verdict the guest
reported through the verdict ABI, in call order: `{seq, kind, label, detail}`;
omitted when the run reported none), `result_line`, `stdout`, `stderr`,
`reports` (Patina's end-of-run report lines, kept out of `stderr`),
`message`, optional native `coverage` (present when a coverage map was
requested) =
`{edges_total, edges_covered, covered_permille, hits_total, hits_max, saturated,
map_path?}`, and `trace` =
`{path, format_version, timelines[], event_count, metadata}` where `metadata` is
the raw trace metadata (seed, faults, buggify, guest_argv, and any future fields,
rendered generically). `trace info --format
json` is a normal `patina.result/v2` envelope with a nested
`patina.trace.info/v1` `trace_info` payload; `trace stats --format json` and
`trace diff --format json` likewise nest `patina.trace.stats/v1` and
`patina.trace.diff/v1` payloads. `trace events --format json` emits
`patina.trace.events/v1` JSONL (header/events/summary; event lines carry raw
`operation`/`outcome`).

#### Runtime-owned outcome fields

A run/replay envelope also carries what Patina itself knows about the outcome,
structurally. These fields, lifted from the runtime's `patina.runfacts/v1`
document, are the machine channel: the `PATINA_*` report lines are for people
and nothing parses them. Every field is optional and ABSENT means "did not
fire", never zero.

- `fault_reports{}` — per-plane accounting, keyed `fs`, `dns`, `net`, `entropy`,
  `clock`, `swarm`, `schedule`. Each object carries the same fields as its
  human `PATINA_*_REPORT` line, including every
  `*_vacuity_diagnosable` bit, the per-op-kind breakdowns (`errors_by_op`,
  `shorts_by_op` as `{kind: count}` objects), and the plane's `vacuous` bit. A
  plane appears only when it saw at least one opportunity. The runtime builds
  these from the report structs the lines are formatted from and hands them over
  as a `patina.runfacts/v1` document, so the two sources cannot drift.
- `replay_divergence` — present on a replay that did not follow its trace, as a
  typed kind: the trace layer's (`trace_exhausted`, `operation_mismatch`,
  `outcome_mismatch`, `unconsumed_events`) or the runtime's own cross-checks
  (`time_model_mismatch`, `schedule_divergence`, `compute_stop_state`).
  Carried on the `patina.runfacts/v1` channel, which
  the guest cannot write, so no guest output can claim one.
- `executable_unavailable` — `true` when the guest looked up its own
  executable (`/proc/self/exe`, `/proc/self/maps`), which the simulated
  filesystem does not hold: a backtrace it printed has no symbols.
- `likely_artifacts[]` — on a run that did not end clean, what points at the
  simulated world rather than the program; beside the class, never changing it
  or the exit status. `{kind: "missing_host_path", path, mount}`: the guest
  opened or stat'ed an absolute path the run was not given and the host has
  (judged by the supervisor after the run, never by the guest), and
  `--mount <mount>` provides it. `{kind: "patina_limit", limit}`: the run
  stopped on Patina's `step_budget` or `compute_bound`. The human format
  prints each as a `patina: likely artifact:` line. It depends on the host the
  run ended on, so it is not part of the run's identity; paths under `/etc`,
  `/usr` and the pseudo filesystems are never flagged, nor are relative paths.
- `sdk` — the cooperative-SUT site accounting when the run declared or
  evaluated a site: `enabled`, `swarm_deselected`, the fire/activation
  permille, `sites_registered`, `sites_activated`, `total_firings`, the
  cutoff and setup-gate state, `declared_sites[]` (`{label, kind, site}`) and
  `sites[]` (`{label, kind, site, active, evals, fires, reachable,
  sometimes_satisfied, always_violated, knob}`). A campaign folds it into
  `sites.json`. `verdicts[]` gathers every runtime context's verdicts in a
  process that ran several (each context numbers its own `seq` from 0).
- `schedule_policy` — the exploration policy's accounting when PCT was
  active (`pct`, `pct_depth`, `pct_change_points`, `pct_change_points_hit`,
  `decisions`, `bug_depth`); `bug_depth` annotates a campaign signature.
- `runtime_findings[]` — runtime-detected findings, each with a `source`:
  `liveness` (a fired liveness/converge watchdog, carrying
  `kind`/`detail`/`vtime_ns`/`budget_ns`/`last_fault_vtime_ns`) and `schedule`
  (`vacuous_schedule` with the unschedulable `tasks[]`).
- `stop` = `{reason, detail, guest_exit_code?, mismatch?, location?}` — what stopped a run
  that did not end clean: `reason` is a stable token, `detail` the line naming
  what was reached. `location` = `{function, file?, line?}` names where a
  compute-bound guest was spinning, from its sampled PC and the executable's
  symbols (`file`/`line` need debug info); absent when neither names it. It
  is a wall-clock sample: two runs of a seed may name different places, and a
  replay names none, so never key on it. The native shim writes one to a supervisor pipe whenever it
  ends a run (its only abort vehicle requires the class and reason: `deny_trap`,
  `not_modeled`, `deadlock`, `liveness`, `step_budget`, `compute_bound`,
  `always`, `sdk_misuse`, `runtime_init`, `shutdown_failure`, `host_limit`,
  `crash_failed`, `shim_fatal`, `shim_panic`, ...); the supervisor builds the
  rest (`prerun_audit` and `trace_mismatch` before any guest launch, with no
  `guest_exit`; `violation_verdict`; `replay_divergence`; `trace_unavailable`;
  `host_kill`; `no_runtime`; `signal`; `panic`, a Rust guest that ended with
  status 101; `exit_status`). A death by signal that the
  shim did not claim is the guest's own `crash`, since the shim cannot abort
  without saying so. The guest cannot write either channel.
- `trace_unusable` — `true` when the class is the guest's own while the run's
  recording was lost.
- `trace_incomplete` = `{reason, detail}` — the recording `--record` asked for
  was not written. `reason` is `resource_limit` (the recording outgrew the
  trace budget, 4,000,000 events or 256 MiB, and was dropped),
  `channel_unavailable` (its scratch file could not be read or moved) or
  `incomplete` (the guest ended before the recording was finalized). A fact
  beside `result`, which a dropped recording never changes: the same run
  without `--record` has the same class.
- `qualifications[]` = `{kind, detail}` — what the operator relaxed for a
  native run, each a reason its determinism is not guaranteed:
  `randomized_address_layout` (`--allow-randomized-address-layout`) and
  `unsupported_symbols` (`--allow-unsupported-symbols` downgrades, `detail`
  naming them). Absent on an unqualified run.
- `guest_exit` = `{code, signal?, signal_name?, core?}` — how the guest process ended.
  `core` is the observed wait-status core flag, present only on signal death.
  `code` is the shell-style `128 + signal` on a signal death, which cannot be
  told apart from a deliberate `exit(134)`; `signal` is what tells them apart.

## SDK macros (crate `patina-dst`, default features = dependency-light SDK)

Instrument a system-under-test; every default-feature macro is a no-op under a
plain `cargo build` (adopters pay nothing) and lowers to the runtime only under
Patina. The default-off `macros` feature re-exports `#[patina_dst::test]` for
dev-dependency use under plain `cargo test`.

- `#[patina_dst::test]`: point-solution DST test. The plain test process finds
  `patina` via absolute `PATINA_CLI` or `patina` on `PATH`, runs
  `patina test` for that one test, sweeps 20 seeds by default (or macro args
  such as `seed = 7`, `seeds = 200`, `buggify`, `net_drop_permille = 50`), and
  panics with the failing seed plus `patina test` / `patina replay`
  repro commands. Missing CLI discovery is a failure, never a skip. The
  arguments are the flags of `patina test` with `_` for `-`, checked when the
  test is compiled: an unknown name, a value on a switch or a missing value
  does not compile. It works in `tests/*.rs` of a package whose own binary
  calls the SDK.
- `patina_dst::buggify!("label")` -> bool: fires on a rare, seed-deterministic path.
- `patina_dst::buggify_with_prob!("label", 0.9)`, `patina_dst::buggify_delay!("label")`,
  `patina_dst::buggify_knob!("label", default, lo, hi)` -> value.
- `patina_dst::always!(cond, "label")`: fatal invariant; a violation reports a
  `violation` verdict (below) and aborts. The verdict is the only announcement.
- `patina_dst::verdict(VerdictKind::{Violation,Pass,AbortIntent}, "label", "detail")`:
  report a structured outcome. One ABI verb; kinds are data. Recorded as a trace
  event (replay reproduces it; a divergent verdict stream fails closed), printed
  as a human `PATINA_VERDICT` line, and surfaced in `--format json` as `verdicts[]`
  (`seq`, `kind`, `label`, `detail`). A verdict changes no control flow:
  `AbortIntent` attributes an abort the guest performs itself. Labels share the
  `sites.json` namespace but register no site, so the duplicate-label rule does
  not apply and repeating a label is how verdicts aggregate.
- `patina_dst::sometimes!(cond, "label")`, `patina_dst::reachable!("label")`: coverage.
- `patina_dst::lifecycle::setup_complete()`, `patina_dst::lifecycle::event!("name")`.
- `patina_dst::rng()`: seed-bridged deterministic entropy. `patina_dst::is_simulated()`.
- `patina_dst::param("key") -> Option<String>`: a run parameter
  (`run --param key=value`), recorded and
  restored on replay; `None` outside Patina.

## proptest

- Stock `proptest` works unmodified under the native shim (`run`, `test`
  harness mode): case generation AND shrinking draw from the run seed, so a
  failing seed shrinks to the same minimal case on every run and on replay.
- Failure persistence is inert: the guest filesystem is in-memory and fresh per
  run, with no host directory visible unless `--mount` (read-only) is given, so
  `proptest-regressions/` is never read or written. Keep the failing seed or
  its trace as the regression record.
- For stateful/model-based tests use `proptest-state-machine`.

## Interpreting results

- Exit 0 = clean. A nonzero exit is the guest's own code; a `violation`
  verdict (an `always!` abort included) classifies as `violation` under
  `--format json`, and printed failure text alone as `failure`. A CLI-side error (bad flags,
  build failure, refused replay) exits 2.
- `PATINA_SCHEDULE_REPORT` (`--verbose`) reports per-task scheduling boundaries and
  warns (`vacuous_threads>0`) when a spawned thread ran zero interposed ops — i.e.
  its interleavings were not actually explored (use `build --instrument` and
  `run --yield-stride N`). A Go guest's threads are never flagged: its meter
  takes scheduling points in any thread running Go code, so a thread without
  one is an idle runtime thread.
- `PATINA_COVERAGE_REPORT` (`--verbose`) reports native edge coverage (`--instrument`, or a Go guest)
  (`edges_covered/edges_total`, hit totals/max, saturation); suppress with
  `PATINA_COVERAGE_REPORT=0`.
- `PATINA_SDK_REPORT` (`--verbose`) reports buggify site registration/activation/firing (the envelope's `sdk` is the machine copy); each `site=` row ends with `|@<file:line>`. `enabled=0 swarm_deselected=1` means buggify WAS requested and this generation's `--swarm` draw dropped it; `enabled=0 swarm_deselected=0` means it was never requested.
- `PATINA_SWARM_REPORT` (`--verbose`) reports the `--swarm` decision for every fault class: `candidates=N selected=M deselected=K vacuous=<0|1>` then one `class=<token>|<0|1>` row per candidate. A class that was never enabled appears in no row. `vacuous=1` means `--swarm` was requested with NO fault class enabled, so the draw had nothing to select and the run explored the plain configuration; the runtime warns and a campaign refuses `--swarm` when it enables nothing to mask. Dropping every candidate of a non-empty set is a legitimate draw (`vacuous=0`). Suppress with `PATINA_SWARM_REPORT=0`.
- `PATINA_FS_FAULT_REPORT` (`--verbose`) reports the filesystem fault plane per class: `eligible_ops=N`, then for each of the error/short/latency classes a `*_vacuity_diagnosable=<0|1>` bit and its applied count, then `vacuous=<0|1>`. The error and short classes each also carry a per-operation-kind breakdown of where their effects landed — `errors_by_op=open:1,read:2`, `shorts_by_op=write:3` — listing only the kinds that absorbed an effect, in a fixed order, and `-` when none did. The breakdown is what the scalar count cannot say: a knob that fired plenty but only ever on `open` left every post-open failure path untested. `vacuous=1` means a class was live over enough opportunities to expect several firings yet applied zero effects (it is silently inert on the exercised I/O path); the runtime warns and a campaign classifies that generation `VACUOUS` with the fs plane in its signature. Suppress with `PATINA_FS_FAULT_REPORT=0`.
- `PATINA_VERDICT seq=N kind=<violation|pass|abort_intent> label=L detail=D`
  (stderr) is emitted once per verdict ABI call, at the call, on every family,
  with `label`/`detail` quoted. Unlike the reports below it has NO suppression
  variable. It is for people; the envelope's `verdicts[]` is the machine copy.
- Every end-of-run report above is on by default and is silenced by setting its
  own variable to a false-y value (`0`, `off`, `false`, `no`), on every family:
  `PATINA_SCHEDULE_REPORT`, `PATINA_SCHEDULE_POLICY_REPORT` (gates the
  `PATINA_SCHEDULE_POLICY` line), `PATINA_SWARM_REPORT`,
  `PATINA_LIVENESS_REPORT`, `PATINA_SDK_REPORT`, `PATINA_FS_FAULT_REPORT`,
  `PATINA_DNS_FAULT_REPORT`, `PATINA_NET_FAULT_REPORT`,
  `PATINA_COVERAGE_REPORT`. Suppression is presentation
  only: it changes no recorded byte and no fingerprint, so a quietly recorded
  trace and a loud one replay against each other. Nothing parses these lines:
  the envelope's structured fields carry the same facts whatever is silenced.
- A trace is compact JSON: inspect it with `jq . run.patina`.
- Debug a failing seed from its recording, not with added prints (they change
  the binary and can change the schedule): `replay` with `-v`/`--render`,
  `trace events --notable`, and `trace diff` against a changed build's
  recording. docs/GUIDE.md, "Debugging a seed".

## Docs

- Validation: `mise run check [nextest arguments]` is the inner loop (fmt, host
  clippy, the tests named; with none, the workspace suite including e2e, native
  acceptance tests and syscall conformance). `mise run check:full` adds the
  other platforms' clippy, doctests, the macros feature test and the ecosystem
  testbeds. CI is the landing gate.
- `docs/skills/patina-dst.md`: tool-agnostic agent skill — what Patina is, the
  capability map, and the method for discovering the current surface (the help
  registry's progressive disclosure, the environment registry, the report
  markers). Start here if you are an agent meeting Patina for the first time;
  come back to this file for exact spellings.
- `TUTORIAL.md`: instrument a program with `buggify!`, sweep seeds, catch a
  planted bug, replay it, and render the timeline.
- `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `VALIDATION.md`: design, and what is validated and how.
- `crates/patina-conformance`: syscall conformance scenarios with the live host
  kernel as the oracle; `cargo test -p cargo-patina --test native_conformance`
  (`mise run conformance`) runs each natively and under patina (plus record/replay
  and strace), and each scenario's declared gaps are the exact current
  host≠patina difference.
- `testbeds/`: real end-to-end guests — `workq` (the flagship durable-work-queue
  demo), `pubsub` (a tokio broker on the interposed reactors), and more; see
  `testbeds/README.md` and each testbed's `run-patina.sh`.

## Native development feedback

`mise run check -p cargo-patina --test native_abi` selects cargo-patina's `native_abi` tests. The other
native targets are `native_conformance`, `native_containment`, `native_raw`,
`native_signals`, `native_trace` and `native_workloads`; use Cargo's test-name
filter for a single proof (one conformance scenario is one test, e.g.
`fs_rw`). All run in `check` and the Linux/macOS workspace-test CI jobs. The full gate
also runs the FIFO/rustix-default/cap-std testbeds. See `testbeds/native-boundary/README.md` for
exact owners and platform limits; Linux-only oracle expectations do not replace
portable native ABI tests.
